rows: Generate count rows of (n, squared), stepping n by step

rows.vgi.doc_llm: Generate a deterministic table of `count` rows with columns `n` and `squared`, where `n` runs `0, step, 2*step, ...`. `count` is positional (0 to 1,000,000); `step` is a named argument that defaults to 1, for example `sequence_table(5, step := 2)`. Rows stream back in batches, so large counts do not buffer in memory.
rows.vgi.doc_md:
## sequence_table(count, step := 1)

`count` rows of `(n, squared)` with `n = 0, step, 2*step, ...`.

Deterministic, so it is handy for tests and demos.

rows.vgi.executable_examples: [{"description": "Three rows stepping by two", "sql": "SELECT n, squared FROM hydrology.examples.sequence_table(3, step := 2) ORDER BY n", "expected_result": [[0, 0], [2, 4], [4, 16]]}, {"description": "Count the rows generated", "sql": "SELECT count(*) AS rows FROM hydrology.examples.sequence_table(1000)", "expected_result": [[1000]]}]

Read every item from a paginated REST API, one page per batch

rows.vgi.doc_llm: Read all items from a paginated JSON REST API at `base_url` and return them as rows `(id, name, category, price)`. Pages are requested `page_size` at a time (named argument, default 100) and streamed to DuckDB as they arrive. If a DuckDB secret of type `hydrology_api` exists its `token` is sent as a bearer token; otherwise the `HYDROLOGY_API_TOKEN` environment variable is used. Rate-limit (429) and server errors are retried with backoff.
rows.vgi.doc_md:
## fetch_items(base_url, page_size := 100)

Every item from a paginated REST API, streamed one page per batch.

Authenticate with a `hydrology_api` secret or the `HYDROLOGY_API_TOKEN` environment variable:

```sql
CREATE SECRET (TYPE hydrology_api, TOKEN 'your-token');
```
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description": "The five priciest hardware items from the public demo API", "sql": "SELECT id, name, price FROM hydrology.examples.fetch_items('https://vgi-starter-api.query-farm.services/v1') WHERE category = 'hardware' ORDER BY price DESC LIMIT 5"}, {"description": "Summarize the API's items by category, ten per request", "sql": "SELECT category, count(*) AS items, avg(price) AS avg_price FROM hydrology.examples.fetch_items('https://vgi-starter-api.query-farm.services/v1', page_size := 10) GROUP BY category ORDER BY category"}]
rows.vgi.result_columns_schema: [{"name": "id", "type": "BIGINT", "description": "Item identifier assigned by the API."}, {"name": "name", "type": "VARCHAR", "description": "Item display name."}, {"name": "category", "type": "VARCHAR", "description": "Item category, e.g. 'hardware'."}, {"name": "price", "type": "DOUBLE", "description": "Item price in US dollars."}]

Summarize categorical land cover inside upstream catchment polygons

rows.vgi.doc_llm: Count categorical raster pixel centres within catchment polygons. Returns class codes, area in square metres, class share of valid pixels, and observed coverage including out-of-raster gaps. Never averages or interpolates class codes. Supply geometry_crs matching the catchment geometry. Join catchment WKB to facility points separately with ST_Covers(ST_GeomFromWKB(geometry_wkb), facility_geom).
rows.vgi.doc_md:
## Catchment land cover

Count categorical raster pixel centres within catchment polygons. Returns class codes, area in square metres, class share of valid pixels, and observed coverage including out-of-raster gaps. Never averages or interpolates class codes. Supply geometry_crs matching the catchment geometry. Join catchment WKB to facility points separately with ST_Covers(ST_GeomFromWKB(geometry_wkb), facility_geom).
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description": "Confirm the entire synthetic upstream area has classified land cover", "sql": "SELECT sum(area_m2), min(coverage_fraction) FROM hydrology.main.landcover((SELECT station_id, geometry_wkb FROM hydrology.main.catchments((SELECT * FROM hydrology.main.demo_input)) WHERE status='ok'))"}, {"description": "Land cover of the intervening drainage between a mid-valley gauge and the demo outlet: per class, outlet catchment area minus the nested upstream gauge's catchment area (1,500 m2 of class 10 and 1,800 m2 of class 20)", "sql": "WITH gauges AS (SELECT station_id, x, y FROM hydrology.main.demo_input UNION ALL SELECT 'mid', 500035.0, 4100035.0), cover AS (SELECT station_id, class_code, area_m2 FROM hydrology.main.landcover((SELECT station_id, geometry_wkb FROM hydrology.main.catchments((SELECT * FROM gauges)) WHERE status = 'ok'))) SELECT class_code, sum(area_m2) FILTER (WHERE station_id = 'outlet') AS outlet_area_m2, sum(area_m2) FILTER (WHERE station_id = 'mid') AS upstream_gauge_area_m2, outlet_area_m2 - upstream_gauge_area_m2 AS intervening_area_m2 FROM cover GROUP BY class_code ORDER BY class_code"}]
rows.vgi.executable_examples: [{"description": "Catchment land cover on bundled synthetic data", "sql": "SELECT sum(area_m2), min(coverage_fraction) FROM hydrology.main.landcover((SELECT station_id, geometry_wkb FROM hydrology.main.catchments((SELECT * FROM hydrology.main.demo_input)) WHERE status='ok'))", "expected_result": [[4900.0, 1.0]]}, {"description": "Land cover of the intervening drainage between a mid-valley gauge and the demo outlet: per class, outlet catchment area minus the nested upstream gauge's catchment area (1,500 m2 of class 10 and 1,800 m2 of class 20)", "sql": "WITH gauges AS (SELECT station_id, x, y FROM hydrology.main.demo_input UNION ALL SELECT 'mid', 500035.0, 4100035.0), cover AS (SELECT station_id, class_code, area_m2 FROM hydrology.main.landcover((SELECT station_id, geometry_wkb FROM hydrology.main.catchments((SELECT * FROM gauges)) WHERE status = 'ok'))) SELECT class_code, sum(area_m2) FILTER (WHERE station_id = 'outlet') AS outlet_area_m2, sum(area_m2) FILTER (WHERE station_id = 'mid') AS upstream_gauge_area_m2, outlet_area_m2 - upstream_gauge_area_m2 AS intervening_area_m2 FROM cover GROUP BY class_code ORDER BY class_code", "expected_result": [[10, 2100.0, 600.0, 1500.0], [20, 2800.0, 1000.0, 1800.0]]}]
rows.vgi.result_columns_schema: [{"name": "station_id", "type": "VARCHAR", "description": "Caller-owned station identity."}, {"name": "class_code", "type": "BIGINT", "description": "Integer land-cover class; NULL if the polygon has no valid raster data."}, {"name": "pixel_count", "type": "BIGINT", "description": "Valid cell centres inside the catchment for this class."}, {"name": "area_m2", "type": "DOUBLE", "description": "Class pixel count times source raster cell area, square metres; pixel-centre approximation."}, {"name": "fraction_of_valid", "type": "DOUBLE", "description": "This class's share of valid observed catchment pixels."}, {"name": "coverage_fraction", "type": "DOUBLE", "description": "Fraction of all catchment grid centres with valid land-cover observations."}, {"name": "status", "type": "VARCHAR", "description": "ok or no_data; unknown land cover is not classified as a real category."}]

Synthetic monitoring station at the bundled valley outlet

rows.vgi.doc_llm: One station in EPSG:32618 at the outlet of demo://basin.tif. The synthetic DEM has 49 cells of 100 square metres each. A matching landcover.tif supports area summaries without network access.
rows.vgi.doc_md:
## Demo monitoring station

One station in EPSG:32618 at the outlet of demo://basin.tif. The synthetic DEM has 49 cells of 100 square metres each. A matching landcover.tif supports area summaries without network access.

rows: Delineate upstream D8 catchments for monitoring stations

rows.vgi.doc_llm: Delineate DEM-derived upstream catchments for monitoring-station rows, then summarize categorical land cover and spatially join facilities with the returned WKB polygons. Flow uses PyFlwDir's depression-filled D8 network. Catchments reaching the DEM boundary or nodata are flagged as potentially incomplete. Projected metre DEMs and explicit input coordinate systems are required. This is drainage analysis, not a flood model. The model fills depressions to spill points and routes one D8 downstream link per cell. Boundary-limited catchments must not be treated as globally complete. Null/invalid station coordinates fail; outside and nodata stations return explicit status rows.
rows.vgi.doc_md:
## Upstream catchments

Delineate DEM-derived upstream catchments for monitoring-station rows, then summarize categorical land cover and spatially join facilities with the returned WKB polygons. Flow uses PyFlwDir's depression-filled D8 network. Catchments reaching the DEM boundary or nodata are flagged as potentially incomplete. Projected metre DEMs and explicit input coordinate systems are required. This is drainage analysis, not a flood model. The model fills depressions to spill points and routes one D8 downstream link per cell. Boundary-limited catchments must not be treated as globally complete. Null/invalid station coordinates fail; outside and nodata stations return explicit status rows.
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description": "Delineate the known synthetic valley", "sql": "SELECT station_id, cell_count, area_m2 FROM hydrology.main.catchments((SELECT * FROM hydrology.main.demo_input)) ORDER BY station_id"}, {"description": "Dominant upstream land-cover class for four gauges on the synthetic valley: the two single-cell side gauges are pure class 10 (west) and class 20 (east), while the nested mid-valley gauge and the outlet are both mostly class 20", "sql": "WITH basins AS (SELECT station_id, area_m2, geometry_wkb FROM hydrology.main.catchments((SELECT * FROM (VALUES ('west', 500015.0, 4100035.0), ('mid', 500035.0, 4100035.0), ('east', 500055.0, 4100035.0), ('outlet', 500035.0, 4100005.0)) AS gauges(station_id, x, y))) WHERE status = 'ok') SELECT b.station_id, b.area_m2, arg_max(l.class_code, l.area_m2) AS dominant_class, max(l.fraction_of_valid) AS dominant_share FROM basins AS b JOIN hydrology.main.landcover((SELECT station_id, geometry_wkb FROM basins)) AS l ON l.station_id = b.station_id GROUP BY b.station_id, b.area_m2 ORDER BY b.station_id"}]
rows.vgi.executable_examples: [{"description": "Upstream catchments on bundled synthetic data", "sql": "SELECT station_id, cell_count, area_m2 FROM hydrology.main.catchments((SELECT * FROM hydrology.main.demo_input)) ORDER BY station_id", "expected_result": [["outlet", 49, 4900.0]]}, {"description": "Dominant upstream land-cover class for four gauges on the synthetic valley: the two single-cell side gauges are pure class 10 (west) and class 20 (east), while the nested mid-valley gauge and the outlet are both mostly class 20", "sql": "WITH basins AS (SELECT station_id, area_m2, geometry_wkb FROM hydrology.main.catchments((SELECT * FROM (VALUES ('west', 500015.0, 4100035.0), ('mid', 500035.0, 4100035.0), ('east', 500055.0, 4100035.0), ('outlet', 500035.0, 4100005.0)) AS gauges(station_id, x, y))) WHERE status = 'ok') SELECT b.station_id, b.area_m2, arg_max(l.class_code, l.area_m2) AS dominant_class, max(l.fraction_of_valid) AS dominant_share FROM basins AS b JOIN hydrology.main.landcover((SELECT station_id, geometry_wkb FROM basins)) AS l ON l.station_id = b.station_id GROUP BY b.station_id, b.area_m2 ORDER BY b.station_id", "expected_result": [["east", 200.0, 20, 1.0], ["mid", 1600.0, 20, 0.625], ["outlet", 4900.0, 20, 0.5714285714285714], ["west", 200.0, 10, 1.0]]}]
rows.vgi.result_columns_schema: [{"name": "station_id", "type": "VARCHAR", "description": "Input monitoring-station identity."}, {"name": "cell_count", "type": "BIGINT", "description": "Number of upstream DEM cells, including the outlet cell."}, {"name": "area_m2", "type": "DOUBLE", "description": "Cell count multiplied by projected DEM cell area, square metres."}, {"name": "outlet_x", "type": "DOUBLE", "description": "Selected outlet cell centre X in dem_crs."}, {"name": "outlet_y", "type": "DOUBLE", "description": "Selected outlet cell centre Y in dem_crs."}, {"name": "snap_distance_m", "type": "DOUBLE", "description": "Euclidean distance from the supplied station to the selected cell centre, metres."}, {"name": "boundary_limited", "type": "BOOLEAN", "description": "True if the catchment reaches the DEM boundary or missing-data boundary; extent may be incomplete."}, {"name": "geometry_wkb", "type": "BLOB", "description": "Upstream Polygon/MultiPolygon WKB in dem_crs; use ST_GeomFromWKB for spatial joins."}, {"name": "dem_crs", "type": "VARCHAR", "description": "Projected metre CRS for catchment geometry and outlet coordinates."}, {"name": "status", "type": "VARCHAR", "description": "ok, outside_dem, nodata, or no_stream_within_radius."}]

Greet a name casually: greet('Ada') returns 'Hi, Ada!'

rows.vgi.doc_llm: Return a greeting for each input name in the requested tone. `style` must be a constant, either `'casual'` (`'Hi, Ada!'`) or `'formal'` (`'Good day, Ada.'`); any other value is rejected when the query is planned. NULL names produce NULL.
rows.vgi.doc_md:
## greet(name, style)

A greeting in the chosen tone: `'casual'` or `'formal'`.

`greet('Ada', 'formal')` returns `'Good day, Ada.'`.
